title.narrative: Sierra Leone Education Multi-Donor Trust Fund (No. TF073453)

description.narrative: The objective of the Trust Fund is to improve the management of the education system, teaching practices, and learning conditions. Activities The activities to be financed by the Trust Fund are: - Bank-executed activities, for which the Bank has implementation responsibility: (a)ASA activities. ASA activities to support the implementation of the education sector plan and the Free Quality School Education Program. (b)Supervision and monitoring. Supervision and monitoring. (c)Implementation Support. Provision of implementation support to Recipient-executed activities. (d)Management and administration activities for the Trust Fund, including but not limited to, supporting Trust Fund related meetings; planning and executing work plans and budgets; managing communications and conducting outreach; disseminating lessons learned; reporting on progress; and monitoring and evaluating the activities. - Recipient-executed activities, for which one or more Recipients have implementation responsibility: (a)Policy, Governance, Accountability, and System Administration. This component aims to strengthen the education system in areas of policy, governance, accountability, and administration for enhanced quality of education services. It will support policy and implementation coherence across the education subsectors and promote strategic initiatives at the country level. It will include the following subcomponents: (a) evidence-based education planning and rationalization, (b) curriculum and assessments, and (c) gender equality and inclusive education. (b)Teacher Management and Professional Development. This component seeks to address the critical teacher quality and management issues facing the country. Both system- and school-level interventions will be supported through three subcomponents. The project will assist data-driven decision making with regard to teacher policy. The component will include two subcomponents: (a) teacher workforce planning and teacher management and (b) teacher professional development. (c)School Level Education Development. This component aims to improve the quality of education and the teaching and learning environment by addressing school-level needs. It will focus on support to improve educational delivery among primary schools and junior secondary schools. Specifically, the proposed project will fund the provision of performance-based school grants to non-private primary schools (offering the full cycle) and renovation grants to improve the teaching and learning environment. (d)Project Management, Coordination and Monitoring and Evaluation. This component will support implementation, coordination and supervision of project activities, including, inter alia, outreach, conducting financial audits, data collection and monitoring and evaluation.
